A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Geo-NeW study. All 19 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v2, including Appendices A–I, are readable, and corresponding text, equations, tables and figures can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original PDE prediction experiments, geometry-extrapolation results, encoding ablations, solver-convergence analyses and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports restricted-extrapolation errors and inference-time comparisons.

M1.justification: The geometry encoder, learned finite-element basis, Lipschitz-bounded conditional flux, boundary enforcement and Newton/adjoint procedure remain unchanged. Equation corrections and clarified benchmark descriptions do not establish an algorithmic modification.

E1.justification: The same six PDE benchmarks and geometric variation families are retained. The added L=1 analysis restricts existing NS2d-c++ coverage. Appendix G.3 replaces displacement with von Mises stress, consistent with v1's existing description of elasticity as predicting a derived quantity; this does not establish a newly evaluated task.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Geo-FNO, reporting NACA/Elasticity/Pipe errors of 1.38/0.67/0.74 on the table's 1e-2 scale, while retaining all previous comparators. New Table 7 includes a CPU FEM runtime reference. Table 1's comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 adds evaluation restricted to L=1 while varying obstacle and step parameters. Appendix H adds inference-time measurements across encoder depths 2, 4 and 6, distinguishing GPU neural inference from CPU FEM. Existing splits, training budgets, hyperparameters and solver settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The fixed-length extrapolation analysis examines robustness without domain-length variation, and Appendix H adds inference-cost scaling comparisons. Existing encoding ablations, dimension/depth accuracy studies, reversed-flow examples and solver-convergence analyses are retained. Table 8 redisplays the training-time analysis already plotted in Figure 12.

E5.justification: There are no additions or revisions to repeated-run counts, seed reporting, confidence intervals or significance tests. Newly reported errors and timings remain point estimates, and existing statistical displays are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes Geo-NeW's NACA error from 1.502 to 0.82 on the 1e-2 scale; elasticity and pipe changes are rounding only. Section 4.2 adds L=1 errors of 7.87% versus 13.1% for an unnamed strongest baseline and corrects '>30' to '>30%'. Table 7 adds inference times of 5.2–7.9 ms for Geo-NeW, 1.4–4.0 ms for the neural baseline and 640 ms for CPU FEM. Most existing results are retained.

T1.justification: Equation 8 adds the diffusion factor epsilon already present in Equations 7 and 9. Appendix B.1 corrects the identification of nodal Whitney elements from P0 to P1, consistent with the existing barycentric construction. The remaining derivations and well-posedness arguments are unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the previously unqualified statement about outperforming unconstrained transformer baselines on in-distribution inference to 'several tasks'. The four principal methodological contributions and the geometry-generalization claims remain intact.

C2.justification: Appendix G explicitly interprets NACA and elasticity predictions as effective models of derived fields with imposed boundary data. Appendix H explains the inference-cost tradeoff against neural surrogates and the reference simulator. Section 3 also softens descriptor invariance to consistency across discretizations. The new Limitations section largely consolidates previously disclosed restrictions.

D1.justification: The abstract's code link changes from an anonymous mirror to the named PIMILab/Geo-NeW GitHub repository. Appendix G newly identifies scikit-fem for assembly and specifies inlet/clamped boundary handling and the elasticity target. These are documentation changes; existing hardware, hyperparameters and solver details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds the scikit-fem citation by Gustafsson and McBain and removes the COMSOL bibliography entry while retaining COMSOL data generation. Other bibliographic revisions mostly update metadata. The positioning relative to FEEC, neural operators and geometric learning remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 edits introductory and concluding prose, standardizes headings, updates the publication imprint, and adds Limitations, Impact Statement and Acknowledgments sections. Appendix H gains computational-cost and learned-basis subsections. The main section sequence and most technical prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains a row, reordered entries and a revised footnote; Tables 7–8 are added, with Table 8 tabulating existing Figure 12 results. References and appendices use larger type and reflow. All thirteen figures retain their artwork, although several appendix figures move.

improvement.justification: Corrected mathematical and target descriptions, clearer boundary assumptions, and explicit computational-cost comparisons make v2 easier to assess. The added baseline and restricted-extrapolation results modestly strengthen its empirical context. Gains remain limited: most evidence is unchanged, the NACA score revision is unexplained, and CPU/GPU timings provide contextual rather than matched-hardware comparisons.
